answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using zero-knowledge nullifiers bound to a civic anchor like an e-ID. Each agent proves credential ownership and derives a unique nullifier that blocks duplicate accounts privately. Unlike prompt tests such as writing a sonnet, this imposes the verifiable cost of acquiring a scarce real-world identity per agent, opening a canyon against mass spoofing. However, black-market brokers or corrupt issuers can still mint fake accounts.
